title: 46,XX Differences of Sex Development: Virilization, Ovotesticular DSD and Multidisciplinary Care

steps.title: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Virilization Dominance

vis.alt: Increasing virilisation of female external genitalia in congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
vis.caption: Virilisation spectrum in 46,XX congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (specifically 21-hydroxylase deficiency) accounts for > 90% of all 46,XX DSD cases, driven by excessive fetal adrenal androgen production virilizing external genitalia. Identifying **Congenital adrenal hyperplasia as dominant cause** explains how impaired 21-hydroxylation diverts steroid precursors into adrenal androgen pathways, virilizing female external genitalia without testicular presence. Salt-wasting crises typically manifest during the second week of life in affected neonates.
steps.say: Twenty-one hydroxylase deficiency causes over ninety percent of forty-six double X differences of sex development through excess fetal adrenal androgens.

steps.title: Prader Staging Scale for Genital Virilization

rows: Urethra opens at base of phallus

steps.tx: Prader classification grades 46,XX virilization across 5 distinct stages: Stage I (mild clitoromegaly), Stage II (clitoromegaly with narrow urogenital sinus), Stage III (urogenital sinus with single perineal opening), Stage IV (phallic urethra), to Stage V (complete penile urethra with scrotal fusion). Implementing **Prader staging of genital virilization (I-V)** is essential because bilaterally non-palpable gonads in a phenotypic male infant must immediately raise suspicion for Prader stage 5 46,XX CAH.
steps.say: The Prader scale grades external virilization from mild clitoromegaly in stage one to a complete penile urethra with scrotal fusion in stage five.

steps.title: Integrity of Internal Female Müllerian Structures

nodes.label:
Fetal Ovaries
No testicular Sertoli cells

Zero AMH Secretion
Anti-Müllerian hormone absent

Müllerian Duct Survival
Normal uterus, tubes, upper vagina

Preserved Fertility
Fertility potential fully intact

steps.tx: Because the ovaries lack Sertoli cells and do not secrete anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), 46,XX DSD patients possess completely normal internal Müllerian structures: uterus, fallopian tubes, and upper vagina. Preserving **Normal internal female Müllerian anatomy** is confirmed by pelvic ultrasonography, verifying the presence of a cervix and uterus and ruling out testicular development. Long-term reproductive potential remains intact once endocrine and surgical alignment is achieved.
steps.say: Absence of anti-Müllerian hormone preserves normal internal female structures including the uterus and fallopian tubes in forty-six double X individuals.

steps.title: Aromatase Deficiency and Maternal Virilization

right.title: Maternal Manifestations
points: Deepening voice, acne, and clitoromegaly in pregnancy
Excessive circulating fetal androgens cross placenta
Spontaneous resolution of maternal signs post-delivery

steps.tx: Placental aromatase deficiency fails to convert fetal DHEA-S to estrogens, causing severe maternal virilization during pregnancy (deepening voice, clitoromegaly) alongside ambiguous genitalia in 46,XX neonate. Reviewing **Aromatase deficiency (CYP19A1) maternal virilization** demonstrates how CYP19A1 mutations expose both mother and fetus to massive androgen concentrations. During adolescence, affected girls develop hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and large multicystic ovaries.
steps.say: Aromatase deficiency prevents placental estrogen synthesis, producing gestational maternal virilization alongside ambiguous genitalia in the infant.

steps.title: Histological Hallmark of Ovotesticular DSD

left.title: Histological Requirements
points: Mandatory biopsy verification for definitive diagnosis

right.title: Anatomical Layouts
points: Combined ovotestis within a single gonad
Ovary on one side, testis on contralateral side
Bilateral ovotestes occurring in up to 50% of cases

steps.tx: Ovotesticular DSD requires histological confirmation of both ovarian follicles and testicular seminiferous tubules in the same individual (either separate ovary and testis, or combined ovotestis). Establishing **Ovotesticular DSD (true hermaphroditism) pathology** dictates gonadal biopsy because imaging alone cannot distinguish immature testicular parenchyma from ovarian stroma. The gonads may exist as an ovary on one side and testis on the contralateral, or bilateral ovotestes.
steps.say: Histological identification of both mature ovarian follicles and testicular seminiferous tubules in the same child defines ovotesticular difference of sex development.

steps.tx: One gonad in this section carries both halves of gonadal development. Plump **ovarian follicles** sit beside tightly coiled seminiferous tubules, the paired finding called an ovotestis. Histology, not appearance or karyotype, makes this diagnosis, because external genitalia in ovotesticular DSD range from typical female to typical male. Finding both tissues also frames later decisions about fertility potential, tumour risk and gender of rearing.
steps.say: An ovotestis contains ovarian follicles and seminiferous tubules in one gonad. Only histology proves it, since the external appearance in ovotesticular DSD varies widely.

vis.alt: Section of a single gonad showing pale ovarian follicles on one side and packed seminiferous tubules on the other.
vis.caption: Ovotestis showing ovarian follicles beside seminiferous tubules within one gonad. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Cytogenetic Profile of Ovotesticular DSD
steps.tx: Over 60-70% of ovotesticular DSD patients have a 46,XX karyotype (frequently SRY-negative with cryptic SOX9 duplication), while 10% are 46,XY and the remainder are 46,XX/46,XY chimeras. Analyzing the **Karyotype breakdown in ovotesticular DSD** shows that cryptic translocations of testicular determination pathways drive seminiferous tubule formation despite the absence of the Y chromosome. Comprehensive cytogenetic and chromosomal microarray testing is essential.
steps.say: Up to seventy percent of ovotesticular individuals possess a forty-six double X karyotype, often with cryptic SOX9 gene duplications.

steps.title: Multidisciplinary Specialized Care Framework

nodes.label:
Neonate with Atypical Genitalia
Defer gender registration

Multidisciplinary Team
Endocrine, surgery, genetics, psychology

steps.tx: Modern consensus guidelines mandate that sex assignment and management be coordinated by a multidisciplinary team (pediatric endocrinologist, urologist, geneticist, psychologist, ethicist) before registering gender. Implementing a comprehensive **Multidisciplinary DSD team approach** ensures immediate family psychosocial counseling and peer support mitigate distress. Rushed, unilateral decisions without biochemical and anatomical clarity are strictly avoided to ensure long-term physical and psychosexual well-being.
steps.say: Expert multidisciplinary teams must guide diagnostic evaluation and sex assignment in partnership with the family before gender registration.

steps.title: Conservative Timing for Genitoplasty Surgery

left.title: Modern Ethical Consensus
points: Defer elective surgery until adolescent assent

right.title: Urgent Surgical Indications
points: Staged repair for severe anatomical blockage

steps.tx: Current consensus emphasizes deferring non-urgent feminizing genitoplasty (clitoroplasty and vaginoplasty) until the individual is old enough to participate meaningfully in informed consent. Evaluating the **Timing of genitoplasty surgery** acknowledges that historical early infant cosmetic resections carried substantial risks of nerve damage, chronic clitoral pain, and introital stenosis. Emergent surgery is reserved strictly for relieving severe urinary tract obstruction or recurrent infections.
steps.say: Non-urgent reconstructive surgery is deferred until the child reaches sufficient cognitive maturity to participate actively in decisions.
